reason: This passage from Job 1 contains no divine complaint about the people. Instead, God (יְהוָה) is defending and praising Job's righteousness to the Satan, asking 'Have you considered my servant Job?' (הֲשַׂמְתָּ לִבְּךָ עַל־ עַבְדִּי אִיּוֹב). God describes Job as 'perfect and upright, one who fears God and turns away from evil' (תָּם וְיָשָׁר וִירֵא אֱלֹהִים וְסָר מֵרָע). The tone is protective and affirmative, not complaining. The narrative concerns a test permitted to Job by God following the Satan's challenge, not God expressing grievances about the people.
